With 6 groups and atoms of the form "value != i", a clause covers a context unless all 4 literals are false on it, i.e., unless the context's value equals all 4 excluded values — impossible since each literal excludes only one value... wait: literal "f0 != i" is false only when f0 == i. A clause is false on a context only if ALL its literals are false → requires f0 == i1 == i2 == ... → impossible for distinct i's. So any clause of distinct atoms covers all contexts ✓.

So why no eligible clauses? The witness condition! For a clause {A_i, A_j} (A_i = f0 != i), the witnesses for A_i: contexts where f0 != i AND f0 == j (A_j false) → contexts with value j → ✓ (each source has such contexts). So witnesses exist ✓.

import sys, time, random
sys.path.insert(0,'/app/submission')
import main as M

rng = random.Random(1)
# Build synthetic class structures: 2000 classes, avg 5 members each
structs = []
for c in range(2000):
    members = []
    for m in range(5):
        lits = tuple(sorted(rng.sample(range(40), 3)))
        members.append(lits)
    structs.append(M.Service._class_structure(members))

tmasks = [rng.getrandbits(40) for _ in range(1024)]
t0=time.time()
for tm in tmasks:
    M.Service._counts_for(tm, structs)
t1=time.time()
print("1024 queries x 2000 classes: %.3f s" % (t1-t0))

# single class with 50000 members
big = [tuple(sorted(rng.sample(range(40),3))) for _ in range(50000)]
st = M.Service._class_structure(big)
t0=time.time()
for tm in tmasks[:100]:
    M.Service._counts_for(tm, [st])
t1=time.time()
print("100 queries x 1 class of 50000 members: %.3f s" % (t1-t0))
